recipes.name: Oreo Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 3 (250 g) packages PHILADELPHIA Brick Cream Cheese, softened

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place 16 cookies in a resealable plastic bag. Flatten bag to remove excess air, then seal bag. Finely crush cookies by rolling a rolling pin across the bag.
Place crushed cookies in a bowl. Add melted butter; mix well.
Press mixture firmly onto bottom of a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until well-blended.
Beat in eggs, 1 at a time, until just blended.
Chop remaining 8 cookies; gently stir 1/2 of the chopped cookies into cream cheese batter.
Pour over prepared crust; sprinkle remaining chopped cookies on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until center is just set, about 45 minutes.
Refrigerate for 3 hours to overnight. Cut cheesecake into 12 equal pieces; store leftovers in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Oreo Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This Oreo cheesecake combines chocolate sandwich cookies and cream cheese with a chocolate cookie crust for a rich, decadent, easy-to-prepare dessert.

review.reviewBody: Good for starting out, but the actual cheesecake filling needed something extra. I added some sour cream and heavy cream to the mixture since it was just cream cheese, knew it needed something else to provide a better, creamier cheesecake. I still think I should have added more, possibly another brick of cream cheese as well as more sour and heavy cream. I made a choc. drizzle for the top of 2 oz. melted semi sweet choc. and 1/3 c. heavy cream. After setting in the fridge the choc. was hardened a bit and I think it really helped the flavor of the cake. I think the recipe is a bit too plain written as-is, needs a bit of doctoring.

This was a very easy and simple to follow recipe. I ended up doing this as a birthday cake for one of my friends. I knew they were going to be a lot of people so I doubled the recipe, which ended up making 2-9” pie pans and a dozen cupcakes. Going by the normal recipe, it calls for 3/4 cup sugar, doubling that is 1-1/2 cups of sugar, so I omitted half a cup of sugar and use the Oreo filling instead which balanced out the flavor of the cheesecake. It was the perfect sweetness for the cupcakes, I used the rest of the crushed Oreo I had for the crust and placed it at the bottom of the cups. This filled half the pan, for the other 6 I used while Oreos as the crust and placed the rest of the cheesecake filling on top of them. For the filling of the cheesecake and the Oreos on top, are used peppermint Oreos which added a nice flavor to it. Upon my little cupcake experiment, both were very good but I opted to go with the crushed crust. I hope you find this helpful!

I, too, made adaptions as recommended by another reviewer. (I def agree with doubling the Oreos, especially for the crust!)! I wanted a "clean" top to decorate for a 50th birthday so, instead of folding cookies into the cream cheese, I spread half the cream mixture on the crust, added a layer of cookie chunks, then poured the remaining cream cheese mixture on top. I reserved a handful of cookies for the final topping. I finely chopped them to dust the top of the cake. This not only concealed the cracks but provided a great backdrop for the other birthday flair I added. Overall, the cake turned out just as beautiful as it tasted!

Easier to serve if you make this into cupcakes, I put a whole Oreo in the bottom of each cupcake paper and pour the batter over top, I also mix 1/2 cup chocolate chips into the batter and then bake same temp but for 25 minutes or until set. Spray whipped cream on top of each cupcake when serving, it's a huge hit!!!

I chose to make these into 12 standard cupcakes using cupcake liners. I found a half a stick of butter worked better for the oreo crust. I doubled the vanilla extract, squeezed fresh lemon juice and added a ½ cup of sour cream to make for a creamier cheesecake. I filled each 18 cupcakes almost to the top and baked them at 275 degrees, rotating pan halfway through, until set in 25 minutes. I turned off the oven, cracked the oven door and let it sit for about 30 minutes. Once the cheesecake cooled I transferred them to the refrigerator for several hours. Probably the hardest part is waiting all those hours until they are chilled. The cheesecake didn’t crack. It’s not too rich, just creamy, smooth and sweet enough. I could see and taste bits and chunks of oreo cookies. I topped these off with, “Sturdy Whipped Cream Frosting,” from this site, and decorated with mini oreo cookies for more visual appeal. These were easy to prepare and I gave them to hubs to share with his crew tonight.
We all loved it! Made it for my mom’s 88th on St. Patrick’s Day so we topped it with green cream Oreos💚and choco ganache….the best!

I made it yesterday, but I made a lighter version of that and when I taste it, it is really light and sweet and even healthier, lighter, and smoother than regular cheesecake and it was because for the crust, I use almond milk instead of butter and for the batter, I use honey instead of sugar and maple syrup for vanilla extract substitution, even though I ran out of vanilla extract, so that what I made a lighter cheesecake.

It’s good but it was missing a little something. It wasn’t quite there yet. I added a ganache on the top of it and it’s perfect! (Melt cream and chocolate chips in a saucepan and cover the cheesecake with it)

Used red velvet Oreos instead. Also, I didn't put my remaining Oreos into the cream cheese/vanilla/sugar/eggs mix...I took the cream out of those cookies, crushed them, and sprinkled them on my baked cheesecake. Also put a thin layer of whipped cream on top ??

This recipe is very similar to the basic cheesecake I use as a base to play with. Used only the chocolate cookie part of the Oreos in the crust with the butter; and added the cream filling into the cream cheese batter.

Absolutely love this recipe. It turned out amazing. I made a homemade cream cheese drizzle to top it. I made it for the residents at assisted living where I work and everyone loved it. 😍 anyone should definitely try this recipe.
It's really easy to do, and its flavor is really nice!!
Was fun to make unfortunately I may have missed or the step to probably let the cream cheese soften or cut it up before mixing would be appreciated lol
I have made this Oreo Cheesecake several times. It is definitely a crowd pleaser.

Loved it! And it’s so easy to make. Instead of the melted chocolate I used up some more Oreo cookies I chopped and the balls were chocolate holes from DD that I rolled and put chocolate sprinkles on. I made this as my dessert for card night. Hope they like it!
I added sour cream to the mix and sprinkled crushed oreos, peppermint dust and a little ground gingerbread coffee to the top. Turned out yummy!! Thanks for a great pie!!!
